newsitem.title: UK: Seasonal slowdown hits commodities, copper lower.
newsitem.headline: Seasonal slowdown hits commodities, copper lower.

text.p: World commodity markets scarcely woke up on Friday after the Christmas holiday as many traders decided to stay away until New Year.
On the London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices finished weak against a background of rising stocks, while also in London cocoa slipped to nine-month lows on origin and light fund sales.
Traders on most markets said activity was unlikely to pick until after the New Year.
Benchmark three month copper futures ended the day at $2,130 a tonne, down $14 from Tuesday, when the market was last open.
The market managed a brief spike higher early on, peaking at $2,165. But a late flurry of selling put paid to the rally.

The LME did not report inventories on Friday because of the Christmas break, and the next data is due to be released next Tuesday. Traders expected stocks to show another increase, encouraging light selling in generally thin conditions.
However, nearby supply tightness remained, with cash copper still holding a strong $100 premium over metal for delivery in three months' time.
Nickel slid to a fresh 2-1/4 year low at the close of $6,476 against $6,480 on Tuesday.
Most other metals were also lower in line with copper.
LIFFE cocoa futures eased to a nine-month low of 888 stg a tonne under origin, trade and light fund selling pressure.
The market managed to crawl back from the lows, with the March contract ending the day nine stg weaker at 891 stg.
Coffee and sugar prices drifted higher in thin conditions.
Oil prices posted modest gains, helped by cold weather and a thin covering of snow in London. Falling U.S. crude oil stocks were also supportive, traders said.
